Empty Space Skipping via Data Structures is a family of volume rendering optimization techniques that reduce computational cost by identifying and bypassing inactive (transparent or empty) regions of a volume dataset before or during ray sampling [S1, S2, S3].

The claim states that 'Empty Space Skipping via Data Structures' is a family of techniques that reduce cost by identifying and bypassing inactive regions. Source [S1] explicitly defines 'Empty space skipping' as a technique to 'reduce the number of times that a ray samples the volume' by 'marching rays only through active volume cells' (bypassing inactive/empty ones) using data structures like 'HistoPyramid' and 'IsoBAS'. Source [S3] describes a method using a 'Mixture Graph' (a data structure/hierarchy) to 'skip longer segments' based on opacity thresholds (identifying inactive regions). Both sources confirm that these methods use data structures to skip inactive regions to improve performance.
supported

**Definition:** A technique achieving extremely fine-grained empty space skipping by marching rays only through active volume cells, located efficiently with a HistoPyramid texture and rendered as point primitives [S1].

The claim accurately reflects the information provided in Source [S1]. The source explicitly states that Liu et al. [LCD09] achieve 'extremely fine-grained empty space skipping by only marching rays through active volume cells, which are efficiently located with a HistoPyramid texture [ZTTS06] and rendered as point primitives'. It further details the acceleration via early-depth testing and front-to-back rasterization, and classifies the method as a hybrid object-order and image-order approach dependent on rendering resolution. All facts in the claim are present in the evidence.
